questions.question_text: A fracture is counted in the bones of the limbs and in the shoulder and pelvic girdles. Which major skeletal division contains these bones?
questions.explanation: The appendicular skeleton includes the limbs and the pectoral and pelvic girdles that attach them.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An anatomical chart shows seven vertebrae in the neck, twelve in the chest and five in the lower back. Which sequence names these regions correctly?
questions.explanation: The typical vertebral formula is seven cervical, twelve thoracic and five lumbar vertebrae, followed by fused sacral and coccygeal segments.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient can nod the head at the joint between the skull and the first cervical vertebra. Which vertebra is the first cervical vertebra?
questions.explanation: The atlas (C1) supports the skull and participates in the atlanto-occipital joint responsible for nodding.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Rotation of the head from side to side occurs largely because the dens of the axis acts as a pivot for which vertebra?
questions.explanation: The dens (odontoid process) of the axis (C2) provides a pivot around which the atlas and head rotate.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A blow compresses the spine. Which structure between adjacent vertebral bodies helps distribute load and absorb shock?
questions.explanation: Intervertebral discs contain a fibrocartilaginous annulus and gelatinous nucleus that help distribute compressive forces.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A vertebra has facets for articulation with ribs. Which region of the vertebral column is it most likely from?
questions.explanation: Thoracic vertebrae articulate with ribs; cervical and lumbar vertebrae generally do not.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient fractures ribs that attach posteriorly to vertebrae but have no anterior attachment to the sternum. Which ribs are involved?
questions.explanation: The 11th and 12th rib pairs are floating ribs; their anterior ends do not attach to the sternum.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A rib joins the sternum indirectly through the cartilage of the rib above rather than through its own cartilage. How is it classified?
questions.option_a: True ribs attach only to the vertebral column and false ribs have no cartilage
questions.option_b: True ribs are floating ribs 11 and 12
questions.option_c: True ribs attach to the sternum through their own costal cartilage; false ribs do not attach directly in that way
questions.option_d: False ribs are part of the skull
questions.explanation: Ribs 1–7 attach directly to the sternum via their own costal cartilage; ribs 8–10 attach indirectly through cartilage above.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A shoulder injury affects the bone that forms the anterior strut between the sternum and the scapula. Which bone is damaged?
questions.explanation: The clavicle connects the sternum to the scapula and acts as a strut that helps hold the shoulder laterally.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A joint permits movement in many directions, including rotation and circumduction, as at the shoulder. Which joint type is this?
questions.explanation: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint, allowing movement through multiple axes and a wide range of motion.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Bending and straightening the elbow mainly occurs at which type of synovial joint?
questions.explanation: The elbow mainly acts as a hinge joint, permitting flexion and extension.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The left and right pubic bones are joined at a midline fibrocartilaginous joint that permits slight movement. Which joint is described?
questions.explanation: The pubic symphysis is a secondary cartilaginous joint that unites the two pubic bones and permits limited movement.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The base of the thumb has a saddle joint. Which movement does this joint make especially possible?
questions.option_b: Opposition of the thumb across the palm
questions.option_c: Only flexion and extension in one plane
questions.option_d: Movement of the ribs during breathing
questions.explanation: The saddle-shaped carpometacarpal joint of the thumb permits opposition, helping the thumb meet the fingertips.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Small movements between adjacent wrist bones occur mainly at which type of joint?
questions.explanation: Many intercarpal joints are plane synovial joints that allow limited gliding movements.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A synovial joint is inflamed and produces less lubricating fluid. Which consequence is most directly expected?
questions.option_a: Increased length of the limb bones
questions.option_b: More friction between moving articular surfaces
questions.option_c: Conversion of cartilage into bone immediately
questions.option_d: Loss of all skeletal muscle fibres
questions.explanation: Synovial fluid lubricates joint surfaces and reduces friction during movement.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is the smooth articular cartilage covering the ends of bones important in a freely movable joint?
questions.option_a: It connects muscle directly to bone
questions.option_c: It reduces friction and helps distribute compressive load
questions.option_d: It forms the hard outer enamel of teeth
questions.explanation: Articular cartilage provides a smooth low-friction surface and helps distribute loads across a synovial joint.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A tissue sample from the shaft of a long bone shows tightly packed concentric lamellae around central canals. Which bone tissue is this?
questions.explanation: Compact bone is dense and organised into osteons with concentric lamellae and central canals.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A long bone’s end contains a lattice of trabeculae aligned with stress lines and spaces containing marrow. Which tissue predominates there?
questions.explanation: Spongy bone consists of trabeculae with marrow-filled spaces, especially in the epiphyses of long bones.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In an adult, which bone marrow is the principal site of ongoing production of red cells, many white cells and platelets?
questions.explanation: Red bone marrow is haematopoietic tissue that produces blood cells; much adult yellow marrow is rich in fat.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A child’s long bone increases in length before the growth plate closes. Which process occurs at the epiphyseal plate?
questions.option_a: Compact bone divides like an epithelial sheet
questions.option_b: Cartilage cells proliferate and are replaced by bone through endochondral ossification
questions.option_c: The tendon turns into a new bone shaft
questions.option_d: The joint capsule lengthens the bone directly
questions.explanation: Longitudinal growth occurs at the epiphyseal plate as cartilage proliferates and is progressively replaced by bone.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which cell type builds new bone matrix during growth and fracture repair?
questions.explanation: Osteoblasts produce bone matrix; osteoclasts resorb bone during remodelling.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During skeletal remodelling, which cells resorb old or damaged bone tissue?
questions.explanation: Osteoclasts break down bone matrix, while osteoblasts form new matrix.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A fracture is immobilised and a temporary callus forms around the break. What is the callus’s role?
questions.option_a: It bridges the fracture and provides a scaffold for repair
questions.option_b: It dissolves the marrow to shorten healing
questions.option_c: It permanently replaces the entire bone with cartilage
questions.option_d: It prevents blood supply from reaching the injury
questions.explanation: A fracture callus stabilises and bridges broken bone ends as repair proceeds and is later remodelled.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person has low bone mass and bones that fracture more easily after minor trauma. Which disorder best fits?
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis reduces bone strength and raises fracture risk; it is not simply inflammation of a joint.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A skull bone is separated from its neighbour by a rigid seam that permits almost no movement. What type of joint is this?
questions.explanation: Most skull bones are joined by fibrous sutures that are essentially immovable in adults.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The lower jaw moves during chewing while most other skull bones remain fixed at sutures. Which bone forms this movable joint?
questions.explanation: The mandible articulates with the temporal bone at the temporomandibular joint and is the principal movable bone of the skull.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A small bone in the neck is suspended within muscles and ligaments and does not form a direct joint with another bone. Which bone is it?
questions.explanation: The hyoid is suspended in the neck and does not directly articulate with another bone.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A climber bears weight through the heel. Which bone forms the heel prominence?
questions.explanation: The calcaneus is the heel bone and is the largest tarsal bone.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A fall lands on the palm and injures one of the eight small bones that form the wrist. These bones are the:
questions.explanation: The wrist contains eight carpal bones; tarsals are in the ankle and metatarsals in the foot.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A surgeon reflects the tough vascular membrane covering the outer surface of a long bone, except at articular areas. What is this membrane called?
questions.explanation: The periosteum covers the external bone surface except where articular cartilage is present; it contains vessels and cells important in growth and repair.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
